newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU ministers underline Turkey's EU credentials.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers underline Turkey's EU credentials.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers told Turkey on Sunday that nothing had changed in its relations with the EU and that it would be treated in the same way as others seeking bloc membership.
"Turkey is...recognised as having a European future and will be judged on the same basis as other countries," Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo told reporters.
Van Mierlo said many problems still remained between Turkey and the EU but that earlier agreements with Ankara were still valid.
These included the 1963 association agreement embracing Turkey as a potential European member and a later opinion by the European Commission that Turkey was not yet ready to become a member.
The foreign ministers were responding to concerns in Turkey that it had been ruled out as a full European partner.
Earlier this month, European Christian Democrats, reacting to Turkish threats against NATO enlargement, dismissed Turkish chances of EU membership in the short or long term.
